message.content:
The famous scene where Del Boy falls through the bar is from the episode **"Yuppy Love"**, which was the first episode of **Series 6** of *Only Fools and Horses*. It originally aired on **8 January 1989** on BBC1.

In this iconic scene, Del Boy (played by Sir David Jason) and Trigger (played by Roger Lloyd Pack) are in a trendy wine bar trying to impress two women. The barman lifts the counter hatch, but Del Boy doesn't notice. As he goes to lean on the bar while telling Trigger to "play it nice and cool," he falls straight through the hatch and disappears from view, while Trigger looks around completely bewildered, wondering where Del has gone.

This scene has been voted the funniest moment in British sitcom history in multiple polls. Interestingly, it was almost different: writer John Sullivan originally wanted Del to simply stumble and catch himself, based on a real-life incident he'd witnessed. However, Sir David Jason insisted on falling all the way through, drawing on his experience in stage farces. Additionally, Trigger wasn't originally meant to be in the scene — Roger Lloyd Pack apparently turned up unannounced on the filming day, and John Sullivan decided to include him, with his confused reaction adding to the comedy.

The episode also marked the first appearance of Cassandra Parry, Rodney's love interest, and featured Del's attempt to reinvent himself as a yuppie.
